competitive_landscape: Inter-island ferries (Bequia Express), a dense charter-yacht fleet, and small inter-island air (SVG Air) move people today — demand proof and partners. The Tobago Cays park favors clean, low-wake vessels. There is no foiling incumbent.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Pioneer II owns the whole island-hopping spine — St Lucia↔St Vincent (~25 nm) and every Grenadines hop (Bequia, Mustique, Canouan, Tobago Cays) within easy all-electric range.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Quanta-LR (H2 2026+) adds the link down to Grenada (~50–75 nm) and any longer southern reach toward Tobago/Trinidad.

precedents.why_it_matters: The Grenadines are the Caribbean's equivalent island-hopping luxury chain.

regulatory_note: Three independent states (St Lucia; St Vincent & the Grenadines; Grenada), each with its own ports authority and customs — a multi-jurisdiction chain. Tobago Cays Marine Park rules strongly favor zero-emission operation.
seasonality: Atlantic hurricane season (Jun–Nov) is the constraint, though the southern Grenadines sit near the belt's edge; the Christmas Winds (Dec–Feb) bring brisk trades that a stabilized foiler handles better than small ferries. Winter–spring is peak sailing.

summary: From St Lucia's Pitons south through St Vincent and the Grenadines (Bequia, Mustique, Canouan, Mayreau, Tobago Cays, Union) to Grenada, this is the classic Caribbean sailing chain — a sequence of resort and yacht-club islands spaced within Pioneer II range of each other. Mustique and Canouan anchor the ultra-luxury end (Mandarin Oriental, Soho House-adjacent), and the Tobago Cays are a protected marine park. The chain is a Pioneer II hop-by-hop network with a Quanta-LR spine.
tagline: The southern Caribbean's island-hopping spine — a string of resort islands within easy electric hops.
